helpful: The provisioned application.txt carried the State's full brief with text extracted, so the merits read came from the filing rather than the docket caption.
CourtListener held the Sixth Circuit's published stay order and dissent within hours of entry; reading the order being challenged was the single most useful retrieval.
The interim statpack section clears the 50-resolved floor for Term 2026, so a committed baseline existed.
gaps: The statpack's interim section publishes no applicant-class cut (state or federal government vs prisoner vs private civil litigant); for a state's application to vacate a stay of execution that cut would move the anchor severalfold and I had to supply it from memory.

fedcourts query has no text, ask-type, or applicant-class filter, so it cannot surface the handful of prior state vacatur-of-stay applications the corpus presumably holds; its granted-applications ranking is dominated by time-extension grants.
No provisioned copy of the lower-court order under review; for an application to vacate a stay, the stayed order is as central as the application itself.
notes: Same-day capital application: the useful horizon between snapshot and disposition is hours, so any retrieval of this docket risks surfacing the outcome. I confined docket retrieval to the Sixth Circuit and district-court dockets.
